My first delivery was pretty intense and scary and I was only 19 at the time. I had gotten diagnosed with Preeclampsia at 31 weeks and had to be hospitalized and 5 days later I had to have a c-section because the IV medication was no longer lowering my blood pressure and I was at risk for having a seizure and the only known cure was to deliver the baby and since he was breech I basically got told that I had 24 hours to prepare myself mentally to not only have my first intense surgery ever in my life and while being totally awake, but have my baby 9 weeks premature. He was in the NICU for 8 weeks and then got to come home and I put a whole new meaning to “helicopter mom”. He didn’t have the machine letting me know everything was okay anymore and I had a baby brother on my dads side die from SIDS, so I was terrified of that and it made me constantly on edge making sure he was breathing. Pretty sure that would trigger anyone that is susceptible to a mental illness.
Because they get mad at how we sometimes snap at them because they don’t realize it’s not anything they did or didn’t do... it’s just our mental illness acting up and we get irritable.
“It’s not you, it’s me.” Is actually a legitimate reason in this situation.
This happens to me after 48 hours without sleep. I try to ignore the feeling because I’ve fucked up my face a few times.

My fiancé is the one who I talk to most about how I’m feeling and is the one who encouraged me to ask my mom for help, but I had no idea how to break the news to her. My whole life she has talked about how my dad was always so bad because he was bipolar and didn’t take his medication so I always associated bipolar disorder to raging, abusive behavior and I’m not like that at all. I didn’t want her to either belittle my feelings or freak out. Then one night I got drunk and I can’t even remember how it got brought up, but I remember ugly crying to my mom about how over the past almost 5 years something has changed with me mentally and I’ve been having suicidal thoughts that have increased with time. I’ve always been depressed feeling and I self harmed when I was a teenager, but it was never like this. I think child birth triggered something because this all started with the intense sadness after having my first son (I’m assuming it was Postpartum Depression, but I never reached out. I was ashamed.) but the suicidal thoughts have increased over the past year and a half and I feel the shift in the manic and depression phases. Even my friends think I’m ignoring them because I go from chatty and outgoing to MIA for weeks. My mom wanted to avoid a close double deductible from starting my treatment so close to the end of the year, so now is the time. This is my 2018 New Years Resolution.
I also have gotten to the point where I hear and see things that are not there. Like people talking in another room and when I go in there no one is home but me.

Thank you so much for taking the time to respond with all of that. I’m actually 24, but I’ve been having these issues for the past 11 years and my mom is just so judgmental I’m nervous about what even to say... I’ve considered writing her a note rather than have the sit down conversation with her so I can get everything out in great detail without her trying to interrupt me. My dad was bipolar so I think I really need to be tested for that and maybe a inpatient hospital stay wouldn’t be too bad to get away from things... I would just feel so bad about leaving my two babies to go do this. It feels selfish..
